Application Materials.content:
Applicants should complete the online application form, uploading all required documents directly. Applications will not be considered until all required documents have been uploaded.
- **Degree certificate(s) and academic transcripts: Required.** From first and subsequent degrees. Degree certificates and transcripts should comply with standard requirements outlined on the guidance pages.
- **Personal statement: Optional.** Personal statements are not required for this programme as they do not form part of the routine application assessment process. However, where an applicant is slightly below the typical entry requirements, the personal statement, if provided, may be used to look for additional context and detail about relevant work experience and achievements. Applicants are welcome to submit a personal statement as an additional document to support their application if they wish.
- **English language certificates/other evidence: Required.** Evidence of meeting the English language profile as stated on the Postgraduate Prospectus and specified by the University English Language Requirements Policy.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV): Optional.** CVs might include details of other relevant work experience and qualifications to support an application.
- If education has been significantly disrupted through health or personal problems, disability, or specific difficulties within studies, applicants can submit an extenuating circumstances form as part of the application.

Interview Requirements.content: Interviews do not form part of the selection process.

Application Deadlines.content:
Start date: **September 2026**
Application deadline: Overseas applicants: **13 August 2026**. Home applicants: **10 September 2026**. Please note that due to high demand, some programmes may close earlier than advertised. Early applications are advised to avoid disappointment. Places are limited and allocated on a continuous basis from **September 2025** until all places are filled.

Academic Requirements.content:
You will typically need an **upper second-class honours degree or international equivalent in any subject**. You will also need to have achieved **60% minimum (or international equivalent)** in at least one of the below modules:
- Applied Statistics
- Mathematics
- Machine Learning
- Data Mining
- Quantitative Geography
- Python or R
- Computer Modelling and Simulation
- Geographic Information System
- Online courses in data science may be considered on a case by case basis.
We will consider your application if your interim grades are currently slightly lower than the programme's entry requirements and may make you an aspirational offer. This offer would be at the standard level, so you would need to achieve the standard entry requirements by the end of your degree. Specific module requirements would still apply.
We will also consider your application if your final overall achieved grade is slightly lower than the programme's entry requirement. If your achieved grade is lower than our entry requirements, your application may be more likely to receive an offer if you have additional relevant work experience or qualifications. If you have at least one of the following, please include your CV when you apply, showing:
- Evidence of **one year's full-time work experience/internship** as a GIS analyst, data scientist or experience in quantitative analytics, urban planning in relevant sectors such as industry, Government or NGOs. Experience must be within the last two years.
- A relevant postgraduate qualification.
Specific module requirements would still apply.
China-specific: To be considered for admission to a master's degree programme at the University of Bristol, the minimum requirement for entry is typically an undergraduate degree from an acceptable institution that is equivalent to a UK upper second-class degree, also known as a 2:1. Qualifications from selected institutions may require accreditation. Applicants who hold a **four-year bachelor's (honours) degree from an accepted Chinese university with a minimum of 78% - 87%** will be considered for admission to a master's degree programme. The required percentage will depend on your undergraduate university and the programme you have applied for.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
For Profile E, applicants need to achieve the listed English language level. Unless specifically stated, the information details the English language skill level required for both undergraduate and postgraduate degrees.
Applicants who are nationals of listed English-speaking countries will generally be exempt from providing additional evidence of English language ability; this is in line with [UKVI guidance](https://www.gov.uk/student-visa/knowledge-of-english). The University reserves the right to ask for additional evidence of English language if there are concerns about an applicant’s abilities.
Applicants who have studied one of the following in an English-speaking country may meet the University's English language requirements: final four years of high school education; two years of a full-time Bachelor's degree; one year of a Master's degree; or two years of a TNE/international partnership degree. **The qualification must have been awarded no more than seven years prior to the start of the degree programme** and completed in an English-speaking country listed by the University. Qualifications completed in Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Singapore, Uganda, and Zambia are also accepted to meet this requirement.
Applicants with a university-level qualification listed above, when fully taught and examined in English in any country, may also meet the University's English language requirements. This must be evidenced by an official Medium of Instruction letter confirming English is the medium of teaching and examination, or an ECCTIS English Language Proficiency Statement confirming the degree is comparable to an English language level of B2 or above.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc in Geographic Data Science and Spatial Analytics focuses on using data and analytics to improve cities and solve spatial problems. Students learn to utilise cutting-edge tools and methods from the data science domain to analyse spatial data and tackle challenges across spatial scales, from neighbourhoods and cities to regions and supra-national systems.
The programme is designed for students from backgrounds in Geography, Planning, Social Sciences more broadly, or numerate subjects such as Computer Science and Engineering. It welcomes students seeking to master data science and machine-learning algorithms, GeoAI tools, and data infrastructures, and apply them to core theories and concepts in social and environmental sciences. Students will employ cartographic and geographic theory and concepts to map and model big geographic data, understand engineering principles around scientific computing and GeoAI, and use them to help tackle global challenges across disciplines.
The MSc builds upon the Quantitative Spatial Science (QuSS) research group within the [School of Geographical Sciences](http://www.bristol.ac.uk/geography/) and its longstanding history and excellence in quantitative geography and spatial analysis. Students join a School ranked **first** in the UK for 'Geography and Environmental Studies' research (_Times Higher Education_ analysis of REF 2021), with weekly seminars organised by the School’s academic research groups, invited speakers, specialist workshops, reading groups, and postgraduate social events.
Key programme details:
- Programme duration: One year full-time; Two years part-time. Part-time study requires daytime weekday attendance.
- Delivery method: On-Campus.
- Location: [Clifton campus](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/clifton-campus/).
- Award available: MSc.
The programme structure follows the data science workflow from data collection and access to data analysis and visualisation. It teaches core skills and knowledge of AI methods, machine learning models, and geographic theories, with a focus on geospatial applications including city science, policymaking, and environmental management. It aims to train the next generation of geographic data scientists who can responsibly use and develop a wide range of methods and tools to tackle pressing societal and environmental challenges. [Visit our programme catalogue](https://www.bris.ac.uk/unit-programme-catalogue/RouteStructure.jsa?ayrCode=26%2F27&byCohort=N&programmeCode=2GEOG002T) for full details of the structure and unit content.
Career prospects: This MSc provides graduates with the skills needed for successful careers as data scientists and data consultants in the private and public sectors. Students have gone on to work in consultancy and in technology and engineering companies, as well as governmental and third sector/non-profit organisations. Many graduates continue in research institutes and think-tanks or pursue further study through a PhD.

Financial Aid.content:
MSc Scholarship Opportunities include:
- [Access Postgrad fee waivers](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/access-postgrad-fee-waivers/): Fee waiver awards towards the cost of tuition fees for students who have completed the Access Postgrad scheme in their final year of undergraduate study at the University.
- [Alternative Guide to Postgraduate Funding Gateway](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/alternative-postgraduate-funding-gateway/): A database of funding opportunities - especially charities - which can make awards (fees, maintenance, research costs) to any student regardless of subject, or nationality.
- [Alumni discount](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/alumni-discount/): Alumni of the University of Bristol can get a 25% reduction in the tuition fees that they pay for postgraduate programmes of study.
- [British Council scholarships for Women](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/women-in-stem-scholarship/): Four fully funded scholarships for female students from Hong Kong, interested in pursuing master's studies.
- [Chevening Scholarships](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/chevening/): Awards to outstanding scholars with leadership potential from around the world to study on a postgraduate course.
- [Colfuturo](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/colfuturo/): An award for Colombian students looking to pursue any taught master's programme or doctoral programme at the University of Bristol.
- [Commonwealth General Master's Scholarships](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/commonwealth-scholarships-general-masters/): Postgraduate scholarships for applicants from low and middle-income Commonwealth countries.
- [Commonwealth Shared Scholarships](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/commonwealth-shared-scholarships/): Postgraduate scholarships for applicants from low and middle-income Commonwealth countries, jointly funded by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC) and participating UK universities.
- [Fulbright University of Bristol Award](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/fulbright/): US citizens can apply for a grant to cover tuition fees and living costs in their first year as a postgraduate at Bristol.
- [GREAT Scholarship 2025: Vietnam](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/great-vietnam/): Funding towards tuition fees for one Vietnamese postgraduate applicant.
- [Marshall Partnership scholarships](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/marshall-partnership-scholarships/): For students from the USA to study at either master's or doctoral level in any subject at the University of Bristol for up to two years.
- [Phyllis Mary Morris bursaries](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/phyllis-mary-morris-bursaries/): A living cost bursary for an international student studying a postgraduate taught programme in the School of Geographical Sciences.
- [R. Senathi Rajah Memorial Scholarship](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/r-s-r-memorial-scholarship/): Sri Lankan postgraduate applicants can apply for funding towards tuition fees.
- [Sanctuary Scholarship](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/sanctuary-scholarship/): Funding for students from asylum-seeking and refugee communities, equivalent to a full tuition fee waiver and a full living cost stipend.
- [Think Big postgraduate award](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/think-big-postgraduate/): Prospective international students can apply for funding towards the cost of tuition fees and living costs.
- [Trusts and charities](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/trusts-charities/): Thousands of trusts and charities in the UK offer small grants or bursaries towards further study or to assist students in financial need.
- [Wellcome Trust grant funding](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/wellcome-trust/): Scholarships and postgraduate funding schemes in the areas of biomedical science, population health, product development and applied research, humanities and social science, and public engagement and creative industries.

Multiple Applications.content: You can apply to more than one postgraduate programme at the University. Simply find your programme using the online prospectus and log in to the application system using your existing username and password.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Requests to defer the year of entry must be submitted via the applicant portal. Requests to defer should be submitted at the earliest opportunity so that it can be reviewed by the admissions team. We cannot guarantee that requests will be granted. Refer to [http://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/after-you-apply/offer/](http://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/after-you-apply/offer/) for more information on deferrals.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Offers made may be conditional or unconditional. An unconditional offer will be made to applicants who have already met the conditions and provided evidence that conditions have been met. Where academic or language requirements have not yet been fulfilled, applicants will receive a conditional offer outlining the requirements that must be met.
Applicants who receive a conditional offer will be required to submit all final results to meet their offer conditions by the date noted in their offer letter. Offer holders who will be unable to provide their final results by this date should email choosebristol-pg@bristol.ac.uk to notify the admissions team as soon as possible.
